property.name: text
property.value:
Set in the Reliquary in the first years after the Angel Bird, when the Children of Light were still what their name said. Folded under the vigil lamp - fifteen nights, fifteen brothers at the bellows and the wick.

The brothers who carried it down did not go back up. Malric's wardens found them in the dark, and found what the blade does to a thing made of Ether: what it cuts, it holds still.

So they drove it into the Sleeper's chest, and the Sleeper slept.

It has fallen out of the wound. The temper line still holds the lamp's light.

property.name: key_name
property.value: Sluice-keeper's Page

property.name: text
property.value:
Day thirty-one since the Eye woke. A month before it did, a stranger with a red lantern came down the old ring shaft and walked straight past the crew, singing.

The outflow above the pit is the only way up to the surface - Brakk's lads saw daylight through it. But the Eye hangs over that pit, and while Malric's converter keeps its basin brimming, its hide is hard as glass. Spears just skid off.

There is one way. The console at the PUMP CONTROL, south of the Sluice Hall, can send the flow down the drain instead of into the basin. Starve it. The shell cracks, and the thing can bleed.

The pump control room is locked. The overseer's key went down that toad's gullet in the vat hall, and Brakk keeps the vat-hall key in the boiler room. Malric took the console's crank back to his laboratory, west.

If you are reading this, I did not make it. Turn the pumps. Get out.

property.name: title
property.value: A Sluice-keeper's Last Page

property.name: text
property.value:
Third time this month the beast tore loose. Bent the bars like reeds.

When it glows and won't settle, open the sluices on the north wall. Cold water drops it every time - it slips, the glow hisses out, and you get a few breaths to put it down.

Never stand in its green spit. Never let it lick the trail back up - it comes out faster.

If the gate goes, run for the valves, not the door. - B.

property.name: text
property.value:
In the corner of the Records Vault, under the cabinets we dragged aside: a stair cut down into the stone, barred with iron, older than anything of ours. Older than Vael. Kroven work - the northmen who were here before the city.

Its lock is a crown with three wheels of crests. Above our own cistern stair the same crests are cut in the gate-stone, in the order the old houses stood at their king's gate: the Anvil, the Tower, the Ram.

I have not turned the wheels. Whatever Kroven locked away down there, it locked away from a king. I have enough kings of my own.

- M.

property.name: lines
property.value: He built that seal with the last of his life. Please - don't be the one who undoes it. | Twenty years he worked down here. I have been sweeping his floor for four hundred. | The Eye cannot call you, can it? You never drank. I knew the moment you walked in - you smell of nothing at all. | If you find his last page, bring it to me. He hid it from the Hierophant. He hid it from me, too.

property.name: lines_1
property.value: I have read it nine times now. His hand shakes on the last line. | Four hundred years, and he finally said it. | Go on. You still have to turn that crank. I know.

property.name: lines_2
property.value: I heard the basin empty from here. Forty barrels a week for four hundred years - and it took you one turn. | The Eye is awake now, and it has your scent. Go, before it learns anything else about you. | If it takes you... I will sweep that floor too.

property.name: lines_3
property.value: You kept his page and broke his seal in the same night. He would have laughed at that. | The Eye is awake. Go. And - thank you, swordsman.

property.name: script
property.value:
say Pell: Don't strike! I'm not one of the mad ones. Not yet.
say Pell: My name is Pell. I kept Malric's books, long ago - his youngest student, before the green made me what I am.|He was a man, you know. A scholar. He wanted every serf in Vael to stand level with the deathless lords.|He did terrible things for it. So did I. I held the knife when we fed the Sleeper.|In the end he chained the Eye with his own dying breath. The pumps, the pipes, the brimming basin - all of it is his seal.|It calls to everything with the green in it. Every night it asks me to open the basin. Every night I sweep a little louder.|You want the crank. It is the only way out, and you will take it. Just... know what you are turning.
say Ren: I'm sorry. I have to get out.
say Pell: He said someone would. He hoped they would at least be sorry.

property.name: script
property.value: set mercy_2\nsay Pell: His hand. I would know it anywhere.|"If this is read, the seal is broken, and I was right to fear it. Whoever carries the Eye now: it cannot take you. Do not let it teach you to want to be taken."|"And Pell - forgive me. You were the only one who stayed."\nsay Pell: ...Thank you. Now go. Get out before it wakes.

property.name: text
property.value:
Forty barrels drawn for the Gift this week. The crew won't go near the cistern anymore.

Lost the pump-room key in the culture vats - the big toad swallowed it before I could fish it out. Sealed the vat hall. Brakk keeps the hall key down in the boiler room, where the brute won't follow.

The old clerk - the goblin who was here before any of us - scratched a mark on the cover: wheel II of the records vault lock.

property.name: title
property.value: Records Vault - Seal Lock

property.name: text
property.value:
Hierophant Absalom came down to us with a body: a spine of white bone, and around it red Ether grown into the shape of a man. No eyes - his men set dead eyes in the vault walls to watch for it. No heart. The thing his people call SPECIMEN ZERO. It breathes. It has never once been anyone.

He wanted my family's relic for it - the left eye, kept in Luke's chest since the year they killed Him. I gave the Eye a body of its own instead.

It sings to anyone who has drunk of Him. Green or red, it makes no difference: not one of the Hierophant's knights could stand before it.

The Sleeper is sealed in this vault. It wakes every hundred years. If the Eye is ever lost, the Sleeper must never learn of it. - M.

property.name: title
property.value: SEALED - The Vessel

property.name: text
property.value:
The Eye drinks and grows. When it is ripe, every serf in Vael drinks of IT - and stands level with the deathless lords.

I keep the crank myself. No fool will starve my Eye.

The records vault lock has three wheels, each carved with old Vael marks. Wheel I must show the mark below. The clerk keeps wheel II in the overseer's ledger; wheel III is on the specimen chart.

property.name: title
property.value: Journal of Malric

property.name: text
property.value:
G-2 - feral. Never feed by hand.
G-5 - feral. Has torn its tether twice.
V-3 - feral. Spits.
V-4 - DOCILE. Odo, my former assistant. Feed weekly. He hid the key to his tonic chest in the old store behind the well - sentimental fool.
V-7 - feral. Hunts by sound.
V-9 - feral.

Anything not marked docile: DO NOT OPEN.

In the margin, in Malric's hand - wheel III of the records vault lock:

property.name: title
property.value: Subject Chart - Cell Block B

property.name: text
property.value:
CROWN ETHER-WORKS - by order of House Vey.

Specimen G-7 'Gorgemaw' broke its tether at the evening feeding. Two handlers lost - and the overseer's pump-room key with them, down the brute's gullet.

The vat hall is SEALED by order of the overseer. The only key to the hall door went to Brakk, chief of the boiler crew: the boiler room is the one place the brute will not follow.

Brakk has not reported back since the Ram broke loose down there.

 - Overseer Grisk

P.S. The courier from the capital asked after the Eye again. Not the Ether - the Eye, and whether it is still whole. I told him it sleeps. He said the King would like it to go on sleeping, unharmed, until it is sent for.
